subject: Technical deep dive recap — latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@nimbushealth.com>, Alex Sullivan <alex.sullivan@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-18T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Technical deep dive recap — latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology

Maya / Alex,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier — really helpful call. As promised, below is a concise recap of the pain points, goals, and the technical items we agreed to follow up on. Please reply with any corrections or additions.

High-level pain points (what you told us):
- Peak latency spikes during clinician triage windows (08:00–10:30 and 16:00–18:00 PST) causing timeouts in your triage microservice.
- Cost sensitivity as usage scales (currently ~75k monthly prompts, expected growth to ~300k within 12 months).
- Data residency & SOC 2 controls required for PHI-adjacent summaries.

Business / technical goals:
- Maintain p95 end-to-end response latency <= 250ms for summary endpoint under normal load; aim for graceful degradation (p99 fallback) under heavy peak load.
- Support sustained throughput of 100–200 requests/sec during peak with burst to 400 req/s for short windows.
- Preserve summary quality comparable to your current 13B model while exploring 7–13B quantized variants to reduce cost.

Model and workload constraints:
- Primary workload: clinical note summarization (single-turn, ~1–2k token inputs, output ~150–300 tokens).
- Preferred architecture: decoder-only LLM (compatibility with current evals).
- Willing to evaluate quantized INT8/4 profiles if quality delta < 3% on ROUGE/clinician-rated metrics.

Deployment topology options we discussed:
1) Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) for predictable throughput + autoscale buffer for peaks.
2) Private VPC deployment (preferred for data residency / SOC 2) with dedicated control plane and optional on-prem worker nodes.
3) Hybrid: Private control plane + Dedicated GPU pools for bursty capacity.

Technical action items (agreed):
- Redwood to propose a topology + latency test harness and initial perf estimates (Marissa / Dev).
- Nimbus to share representative sample of inputs (anonymized) and peak traffic patterns (Alex).
- Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive to walk through expected test plan and run a guided perf run (Marissa to send calendar link).

Attachments: I’m attaching the quick MAU/traffic estimate you shared in the call and a rough architecture sketch we drew during the meeting.

Next steps / proposed owners:
- Alex: share anonymized sample dataset + traffic profile (by Wed 11/25).
- Marissa: send calendar for deep-dive & share perf harness doc (today).
- Dev (cc’d) & Rishi: prepare initial topology options and perf assumptions (before deep-dive).

If that all looks right I’ll schedule the deep-dive for next week. Thanks again — excited to dig in.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

- Peak throughput: we should plan for sustained ~200 req/s during the busiest windows and allow short bursts up to ~450 req/s for scheduled batch ingest.
- Retention / compliance: we require SOC 2 controls and can keep PHI-adjacent data in our VPC; interested in your Private offering with KMS integration.
- Observability: important to have per-request token-level latency & cost breakdowns so we can correlate clinician experience to cost tiers.

I’ve attached a short data-flow diagram and a sanitized sample of 500 notes (anonymized). Alex will upload the full traffic CSV later today.

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Technical deep dive recap — latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology

Working notes for the deep-dive — sharing initial perf assumptions and recommended test plan. Happy to expand during the call.

Recommended candidate configs (ballpark):
A) Dedicated (predictable, high-throughput)
- Base: 4x NVIDIA A100 80GB (reserved) with continuous batching and KV prefix caching.
- Expected steady-state: ~150–200 req/s @ p95 ~180–230ms for a 13B FP16 model with batching tuned to 40–80ms wall-time.
- Burst plan: autoscale to 8x A100 for short windows (up to 450 req/s) with warm KV caches.

B) Private VPC (security + data residency)
- Base: 6x NVIDIA A10 / A30 (cost-effective) + optional on-prem worker pool for residency.
- Expected steady-state: ~100–150 req/s @ p95 ~220–300ms for a quantized 13B INT8 profile; 7B INT4 could reduce latency/cost but needs eval on quality.

Model & quantization notes:
- Start with 13B FP16 baseline to measure quality/perf, run comparisons with 13B INT8 and 7B INT4 quantized variants.
- We’ll produce clinician-rated quality diffs and ROUGE metrics; acceptance threshold is <= 3% delta.

Perf test plan (what we’ll run in the deep-dive):
1) Baseline run: synthetic traffic + 1k real anonymized samples (single-run, no caching) to capture cold-start.
2) Warm-cache run: repeated prefix patterns to measure steady-state with KV caching enabled.
3) Burst test: ramp to 450 req/s for 5–10 minutes to validate autoscale behavior and graceful degradation.
4) Latency breakdown: tokenization, model inference, post-processing, network (per-token traces).

Instrumentation / metrics to capture:
- p50/p95/p99 latencies (end-to-end and model-only)
- tokens/sec, GPU utilization, batch sizes, KV hit-rate
- per-request cost estimate (token-level) and request-level traces for debugging

Docs / links: I’ll drop a detailed perf harness and the runbook into the shared Drive before the call: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2B3C_nimbus-architecture

Next steps I’m proposing:
- Marissa to confirm deep-dive slot: I’m available 11/24 (09:00–12:00 PST) and 11/25 (13:00–16:00 PST).
- Nimbus to upload the full traffic CSV and confirm anonymization (Alex).
- I’ll prepare two config slides (Dedicated vs Private) and a perf-run checklist.
